Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are making their way out to the middle now. Smriti Mandhana and Richa Ghosh are the two openers for India Women. Megan Schutt to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Arundhati Reddy was the star performer for India Women, delivering an exceptional spell of 4/26 in her 10 overs, the best figures ever by a visiting bowler at this ground. Unfortunately, the rest of the bowling attack struggled to contain the Australian batters, with dropped catches and erratic lines proving costly. India Women now face a steep challenge to chase down 299 and salvage some pride in this series. Stay tuned as the action continues with their reply.

Opting to bat first, Australia Women started strong, with openers Phoebe Litchfield and Georgia Voll displaying excellent stroke play. The pair cruised to 58/0 by the end of the Powerplay 1, putting India Women on the back foot. However, Arundhati Reddy turned the game around with a fiery spell, dismissing Voll and Litchfield in the same over. She followed it up by removing Ellyse Perry for just 4 and Beth Mooney for 10, leaving Australia struggling at 78/4 by the 17th over. Annabel Sutherland and Ashleigh Gardner then steadied the ship with a crucial 96-run partnership. Both batters capitalized on early reprieves, with Gardner reaching a well-deserved fifty before falling to Deepti Sharma in the 34th over. Sutherland, however, continued to dominate, unleashing powerful strokes to bring up her second ODI century. She was eventually run out for a brilliant 110 in the final over, while McGrath remained unbeaten on 56, adding late impetus to push the total close to 300.

Australia Women finish just short of the Three Hundred mark and it has been a brilliant performance with the bat from them. Australia Women managed 298/6 after 50 overs, setting a huge target of 299 for India Women at almost 6 runs per over. Australia Women have posted a formidable total of 298/6 in their 50 overs, setting a new record for the highest team score in a Women’s ODI at this venue. The innings was anchored by a stunning century from Annabel Sutherland, with significant contributions from Ashleigh Gardner and Tahlia McGrath. India Women, plagued by missed chances and inconsistent bowling in the latter half of the innings, now face a daunting chase to avoid a series whitewash.

As the series finale approaches, India Women face the challenge of regrouping and delivering a spirited performance to salvage pride. Will they rise to the occasion, or will Australia Women extend their home dominance with another commanding display? Stay tuned for the Toss and other match updates!

India’s response began with an injury-induced shuffle in their batting order, as Richa Ghosh replaced Priya Punia at the top alongside Smriti Mandhana. However, Mandhana’s struggles continued as she was bowled for just 9 by Kim Garth. Ghosh embraced her new role with a fluent half-century, providing a glimmer of hope for India. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues also showed promise, scoring 38 and 43, respectively, but neither could convert their starts into the significant contributions needed to chase the imposing target. India ultimately managed 249/9 in 44.5 overs, falling well short of the total.

In the second match, Australia Women dominated after opting to bat first at the same venue where India struggled to reach 100 in their previous outing. Openers Phoebe Litchfield and Georgia Voll showcased exceptional form, building a commanding 130-run partnership. The caravan moves to Perth, where the iconic W.A.C.A. Ground is set to host the third and final ODI of the series between Australia and India. Dominant in the first two matches, Australia have shown exactly why they are the reigning ODI champions. In the second ODI, centuries from Georgia Voll and Ellyse Perry propelled the hosts to 371, their highest ODI total against India. The target proved to be a mountain too steep to climb as the hosts completed a 122-run win. While their batting faltered in the first ODI, it was the bowling that let the Indians down in the second game. Avoiding a whitewash will require a marked improvement from the tourists. Priya Punia’s availability remains uncertain after a niggle prevented her from batting in the last match. If she misses out, India must decide whether to continue with Richa Ghosh as an opener alongside Smriti Mandhana or experiment with a new combination. Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues have shown promise but must capitalize on their starts to make a meaningful impact. On the bowling front, conceding 371 runs highlights areas that need addressing. Renuka Singh Thakur, Saima Thakor, and leg-spinner Priya Mishra will aim to deliver an improved performance as they build confidence ahead of the upcoming series against the West Indies. As far as Australia are concerned, even with the series already secured, they are unlikely to ease off the accelerator. With a 13-member squad, they have limited room for rotation, but they will still look to make a few adjustments. Darcie Brown who is yet to feature, could potentially get a game, with either Kim Garth or Megan Schutt making way for her in the playing XI. There could also be some shuffling in the batting order, as players like Annabel Sutherland, Ash Gardner, and captain Tahlia McGrath have had limited time in the middle so far. With important series ahead, including an ODI series in New Zealand and the Ashes early next year, Australia might use this game to test their squad's flexibility and give players valuable middle-order exposure. Will India salvage pride and end the series on a positive note, or will Australia complete a dominant clean sweep? We shall find out together.
